planting.note: Set out container plants in spring once soil is workable; tolerates very cold winters down to zone 2.

directions: This compact shrubby cinquefoil opens golden-yellow, fully double flowers that keep coming from early summer through fall. It forms a tidy, rounded mound of bright green foliage reaching about two to three feet in both height and width, making it a good fit for foundation plantings or massed borders. It is bred for toughness in harsh winter climates, needs only occasional watering once established, and is largely ignored by deer while still drawing in pollinators.
sources: First Editions Plants (firsteditionsplants.com) — Pineapple Tart Potentilla product page

planting.note: Plant in spring in average to consistently moist, well-drained soil; prune after flowering since bloom occurs on old wood.

directions: PowFume is a semi-evergreen viburnum that opens large, intensely sweet-scented white flower clusters in early spring, holding its dark green leaves later into the season than many other fragrant viburnums. It grows into a dense, upright, rounded shrub six to eight feet tall, suited to use as a hedge or a stand-alone focal point. The flowers are a strong draw for early-season pollinators, and the plant has a reputation for being left alone by deer.
sources: First Editions Plants (firsteditionsplants.com) — PowFume Viburnum product page

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring with morning sun and afternoon shade; keep soil evenly moist.

directions: DreamCloud is a compact reblooming mophead hydrangea with fully double, densely packed white flower heads that give each bloom a cloud-like fullness. It flowers on both old and new wood, so it keeps producing color from early summer well into fall, and its white blooms resist the browning that affects many other white hydrangea cultivars, sometimes aging to soft pink in certain climates. The plant forms an upright, rounded shrub of dark green foliage reaching three to four feet, and it shows improved resistance to Cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew compared to older varieties. It does best with morning sun and afternoon shade plus consistently moist soil.
sources: Endless Summer Hydrangeas / Bailey Nurseries (endlesssummerhydrangeas.com) — DreamCloud Reblooming Hydrangea product page
